recs.stt: Why did science fiction stop moving forward?
recs.x:
You only notice the bad CGI - most TV shows, even a normal sitcom, have a ton of CG that you would never realize unless you saw the raw shots. It's what the audience expects and demands today. Things are getting more efficient but quality level has risen even faster.

Here's a good video, from 2009: [link]

recs.stt: Jeffrey Katzenberg Says A.I. Will Eliminate 90% of Artist Jobs on Animated Films
recs.x: Even today, there's good and bad uses of CG, usually coming down to schedule and creative direction. The average quality has gone up substantially, though. As you pointed out, there's all kinds of ways to use CGI and VFX more subtly that most people would never realize. [link] is a great example of green screen set replacement being used for things as ordinary as a city street, 15 years ago on a TV series budget.
